title: MAC-LTE and MAC-NR: Fix some cases where same filter can have different strings

notes.body: @pquantin - do these look ok to you? I didn't change all of the LTE NB ones, but I suppose a given capture/log is going to be NB or not...

Hi Martin,

I *think* this was initially done on purpose so that people could easily filter on a given value whether it is using extended variant or not, etc. Is this creating any kind of issue? If yes then I agree it should be changed.
Regarding NB-IoT, you can easily have both NB-IoT and LTE in the same capture as an eNB can support both at the same time.

It can create some issues filtering or using the Filter Expression dialog, somewhat like #19111. E.g., you can filter `mac-lte.control.bsr.buffer-size == "10 < BS <= 12"` but not `mac-lte.control.bsr.buffer-size == "10 < BS <= 13"`.

I think these are not as bad as #19111, because the value strings are different, but at least for values 0 and 1 the same string is used, and for the other values the strings are at least unique. Thus this case could be resolved by doing the reverse mapping over all the value strings of the same filter field in these cases.

In TLS, SSL2 and later versions both use "Server Hello" but with different values, and `tls.handshake.type == 'Server Hello'` ended up matching SSL2 `Server Hello` messages but not ones from later versions.
